# Independent audit of the free and relative container notes

Audited in full:

* `candidate 75212e124d66e084`
* `candidate 870e8284d5328056`

Result: PASS after one literal affine-definition correction, applied by
the author. Both exact symbolic verifiers pass in the SymPy runtime.

## Corrected halfspace definition

The first note originally introduced q_v by an absolute-value formula
and used it in expressions called ambient halfspaces. That formula is
affine only on the cube. It now defines the global affine function

    q_v(z)=sum_j[(1-v_j)z_j+v_j(1-z_j)],

which equals the distance formula on [0,1]^2. All calculations remain
unchanged, and the displayed caps are actual ambient halfspaces.

## Free-container argument

The four interval fibers and their total mass eight are exact. The
own-fiber cap bound, edge-midpoint depth certificates, and two continuous
displacements from the ordinary center establish the stated actual
full-dimensional depth region. The rational corner inequalities follow
from explicit oblique caps of mass below one fifth, so no presumed shape
of the depth region is used.

The added tall vertices of P_R have first coordinate one half. Convex
combinations at the extreme first coordinates zero and one therefore
cannot use them, preserving the two boundary sections that exclude all
integer points. The displayed quadrilateral has area R. This proves
unbounded container volume for a fixed actual depth-region projection.

The facet derivative uses unit normals only at the initial polytope;
arbitrary small changes in normal length cause no missing first-order
factor. For a single-facet variation, lattice points on intersections
with other facets remain excluded by an unchanged facet. The only new
constraints concern relative-interior lattice contacts. All remaining
lattice points are controlled uniformly in a common bounded ball.
Those constraints are exactly linear in the chosen perturbation, so
the Farkas cone is an actual feasible cone, not an assumed tangent cone.
Its coefficient signs give the stated nonnegative contact weights.

The vector, matrix, and trace divergence identities have the displayed
orientations and coefficient n. Physical affine variations must check
every boundary lattice point via at least one containing facet; the
current note explicitly retains that requirement. The inward homothety
strictifies nonpositive first-order margins because the reference point
is interior. No lattice-preserving coordinate change is misused as a
continuous base deformation.

The diamond example satisfies the contact equations and fixed-direction
offset maximality. Its explicit free-normal deformation has second
derivative four and larger area. Thus it does not satisfy the stronger
free-shape local-maximum hypothesis. The note preserves that distinction.

## Relative-container argument

The offset interval bounds are equivalent to containing K after
discarding redundant excess offsets. Interior lattice exclusion is
closed in this compact parameter box. The limiting-set inclusion and
continuity from above prove upper semicontinuity of volume, including
zero-volume limits, so the stated maximum is attained.

A proper new facet admits a positive-volume outward offset variation
unless an integer point lies in its relative interior and in int(P).
Points on other cuts or on the outer boundary remain excluded. Fixed
normal variations give an integer contact, but not a facet-centroid
identity; that limitation is correctly maintained.

The positive continuous-fiber assertion at an interior projection point
follows by interpolating a lifted endpoint with an interior continuous
ball. It also proves that q<d forces the projection to be hollow: any
interior integer projection point would force q=d. Thus the intrinsic
measure in that case lies over boundary indices.

The new-facet and inherited-boundary decomposition retains the complete
outer vector and matrix terms. The scalar trace is exactly n|L|, and
every supporting distance from q in int(L) is positive. The formulas for
moving free planes are identities for those specified motions, not an
assertion of feasibility under the fixed-direction optimization. Planes
coincident with positive-area outer facets are assigned to the outer
boundary; inward motion of such a redundant plane requires a separate
nonsmooth contribution, as the note explicitly states.

The closed vertical support-cap formula includes each boundary fiber
in full. Its threshold jump is exact because only finitely many integer
fibers exist. The square example has no new facets at its attained
relative optimum; all scalar stress is Phi_P=2 and all mixed measure
lies on the projection boundary. The corner-cut formulas

    |L_epsilon|=1-2epsilon^2,
    Phi_P=2-4epsilon,
    2|L_epsilon|=4epsilon(1-epsilon)+Phi_P

are exact, while every positive truncation removes every integer fiber.
Consequently the boundary term cannot be suppressed through ordinary
volume convergence or an assumption that boundary fibers have zero mass.

Neither note establishes an OC cap-budget estimate from these container
identities. Their exclusions and conditional conclusions are correctly
separated.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
